Source: Houston-Galveston Area Council 8 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2.4 AMD as an Integrated System of Networks Since the publication of the second edition, public agencies have increased the adoption of ODT services, rapidly proliferating across urban, suburban, exurban, and rural communities and providing community circulation and FMLM connectivity to regional transit services. ODT is quickly setting the expectation that future public mobility service will, at its base, provide app- based, dynamic, on-demand service for local community circulation—using both commercial entities (TNCs) and services provided by or through a public authority. Having ODT as the foundational mode in an AMD has several implications for operational management, station operations, and infrastructure. The Phase III research has drawn from previous analytical studies of a fully automated type of transit technology that is specifically designed to provide the on-demand class of dispatching in real time for direct origin-to-destination service on a network of fixed guideways. The ANSI/ASCE/T&DI 21-21 Automated People Mover Standards (2021 edition) has named this class of technology “automated transit network” (ATN) systems. These ATN analytical studies, dating from the 1990s to the 2010s, provide insight into AMD networks with respect to the impacts of ridership demand patterns, operational concepts, system configuration, and station management when an AMD includes ODT-type services. The lessons learned from these ATN studies are referenced in this third edition at high summary level, with the next edition in the report series containing a more detailed explanation of the relevant applications to AV fleet operations in AMDs. NLR’s AMD research includes multiple types of public transport services using AV technology across this full spectrum of vehicle types, service modes, and dispatching methods to assess the ramifications for large-scale AMD implementation. As described throughout this report, the AMD concept envisions multiple AV operating fleets, each with different vehicle sizes and service modes, which will likely involve a blend of public and private companies managing the multifleet operations. To reflect this concept as a “system of systems,” the term AMD network system is introduced to describe this whole spectrum of solutions involving transport technology and fleet operations. It includes the anticipation of ODT services at the foundation providing local community circulation and FMLM connectivity to regional mobility services that are blended into a complete mobility system.
